title: Stop hook re-fires identically every turn with no way to resolve without user input, causing a loop
details:
**What happened:** A `check_functional_docs.py` Stop hook fired 4 consecutive turns with byte-identical output, after the assistant explicitly declined to act (uncommitted changes in the shared checkout belonged to another party, not the assistant) and asked the user a clarifying question. No new user message arrived between fires — each "user" turn was just the same hook payload again.
**What the user said:** User didn't comment; observed by the model. No human reply appeared between the repeated hook firings.
**Repro:** Have uncommitted functional-file changes in a repo (from any source) with a `documenter-changement-fonctionnel`-style Stop hook configured; end an assistant turn without committing or calling the hook's own `--ack` escape hatch (e.g. because the assistant correctly judged the changes weren't its own to acknowledge); the hook re-fires with identical content on every subsequent Stop even when the assistant's reply already addressed it and is only waiting on the user.
**Evidence:** Session this occurred in; hook script path `.claude/skills/documenter-changement-fonctionnel/scripts/check_functional_docs.py`.
**Cause:** The hook appears to have no "already surfaced this turn, don't repeat until state changes or the user responds" gate — it re-evaluates and re-prints on every Stop unconditionally.
